title: Computer Graphics
description: Applications of computer graphics, including simulation, robotics and aerial mapping; graphics hardware and software; output primitives and line and circle drawing; polygons, polygon filling and meshes; two- and three-dimensional transformations; 3D modelling, viewing and rendering; and computational geometry. The folder has only the 2023/24 paper, so every topic is written from general knowledge of a standard computer graphics course and labelled so.

topics.title: Introduction and Applications of Computer Graphics
topics.summary: Computer graphics creates, stores and manipulates images by computer, in raster or vector form. It is used in design, entertainment, visualisation, simulation and training, robotics and the automatic mapping of buildings from aerial images.
subtopics: What computer graphics is; raster and vector images
Building detection and mapping from aerial images

topics.title: Graphics Hardware and Software
topics.summary: Graphics systems display images on raster screens refreshed from a frame buffer and drawn by a graphics processing unit. Choosing a workstation involves the CPU, RAM, storage, graphics card and monitor, and graphics software ranges from APIs such as OpenGL to design and collaboration tools.
subtopics: Frame buffer, resolution, colour depth and refresh
Workstation choice: CPU, RAM, storage, graphics card, monitor

topics.title: Output Primitives and Line and Circle Drawing
topics.summary: Output primitives are the basic elements of a picture: points, lines, circles, polygons and text. Scan-conversion algorithms such as DDA, Bresenham's line algorithm and the midpoint circle algorithm decide which pixels to light.
subtopics: The midpoint circle algorithm and symmetry

topics.title: Shapes, Polygons and Polygon Filling
topics.summary: Shapes and polygons are the building blocks of graphics models: convex and concave polygons, triangles and polygon meshes. Areas are filled by scan-line, boundary-fill and flood-fill algorithms, and polygons are clipped to the viewing window.
subtopics: Inside-outside tests: even-odd and winding-number rules

topics.title: Geometric Transformations
topics.summary: Transformations move and reshape objects: translation, scaling, rotation, reflection and shear. Homogeneous coordinates write them all as matrices, so sequences of transformations combine into one composite matrix, in two and three dimensions.
subtopics: Composite transformations; rotation about a point

topics.title: 3D Modelling, Viewing and Rendering
topics.summary: 3D models are built from polygon meshes, curves and surfaces, then viewed through parallel or perspective projection. Rendering removes hidden surfaces and applies lighting, shading and texture to produce realistic images, as in film creatures.
subtopics: Curves and surfaces: Bézier and B-splines
Hidden-surface removal: z-buffer and back-face culling
Lighting and shading: flat, Gouraud, Phong

topics.title: Computational Geometry
topics.summary: Computational geometry develops efficient algorithms for geometric problems: convex hulls, segment intersection, point location, triangulation and Voronoi diagrams. Its applications include robot motion planning, obstacle avoidance and localisation, GIS, computer-aided design and graphics.
subtopics: Convex hulls: Graham scan, gift wrapping
Triangulation, Delaunay triangulation and Voronoi diagrams
Robot motion planning: configuration space, visibility graphs
